verses.1: A psalm of David. Give to the LORD, you heavenly beings, give to the LORD glory and might;
verses.2: Give to the LORD the glory due God's name. Bow down before the LORD'S holy splendor!
verses.3: The voice of the LORD is over the waters; the God of glory thunders, the LORD, over the mighty waters.
verses.4: The voice of the LORD is power; the voice of the LORD is splendor.
verses.5: The voice of the LORD cracks the cedars; the LORD splinters the cedars of Lebanon,
verses.6: Makes Lebanon leap like a calf, and Sirion like a young bull.
verses.7: The voice of the LORD strikes with fiery flame;
verses.8: the voice of the LORD rocks the desert; the LORD rocks the desert of Kadesh.
verses.9: The voice of the LORD twists the oaks and strips the forests bare. All in his palace say, "Glory!"
verses.10: The LORD sits enthroned above the flood! The LORD reigns as king forever!
verses.11: May the LORD give might to his people; may the LORD bless his people with peace!

notes.text: You heavenly beings: literally "sons of God," i.e., members of the heavenly court who served Israel's God in a variety of capacities.

The voice of the LORD: the sevenfold repetition of the phrase imitates the sound of crashing thunder and may allude to God's primordial slaying of Leviathan, the seven-headed sea monster of Canaanite mythology.
Sirion: the Phoenician name for Mount Hermon. Cf Deut 3:9.
The desert of Kadesh: probably north of Palestine in the neighborhood of Lebanon and Hermon.
The flood: God defeated the primordial waters and made them part of the universe. Cf Psalm 89:10-13; 93:3-4.
